title: Meet Cargo NS-01 and TTF-Q1: the two trades you will follow
story: Sam puts two printed trade tickets on your desk. *"From today, these two are yours. Chris bought a North Sea cargo yesterday, and Dana bought gas for next winter. You will follow them every week: their price, their risk, their P&L, their invoices. When you know their whole life, you know the job."* Chris adds: *"And yes, it is the 600,000 barrels from your first week."*
objective: I can read the key data of a physical oil trade and a gas trade, and value the gas trade with the forward curve.

write.heading: 1. Cargo NS-01 (Chris, crude oil)
write.body:
| Field | Value (illustrative) |
|---|---|
| Direction | Buy |
| Quantity | 600,000 bbl North Sea crude |
| Price | Dated Brent + 0.50 USD/bbl |
| Delivery | loading next month, on an Aframax (→ L19) |

Chris hedges the price risk by selling 600 Brent futures (1 lot = 1,000 bbl) (→ L5).

write.heading: 2. TTF-Q1 (Dana, gas)
write.body:
Dana buys **1,000 MWh per day** of TTF gas for **Q1** (January to March, 90 days).
Total = 1,000 × 90 = **90,000 MWh** at **35 EUR/MWh** (example).

write.heading: 3. Valuing TTF-Q1
write.body:
Tonight the Q1 tenor of the TTF curve (→ L13) is 37 EUR/MWh (example).
MtM = (37 − 35) × 90,000 = **+180,000 EUR**. Dana bought, the price went up: a gain, not yet realised.

write.heading: 4. Middle office check
write.body: Every trade needs the same key fields: trade ID, direction, product, quantity and unit, price, delivery period and place, counterparty, book (→ L1). One missing field = a wrong report tomorrow.

check.q: How many Brent futures lots hedge 600,000 bbl, and should Chris buy or sell them?
check.a: 600 lots (600,000 / 1,000). Chris sells them: the desk owns the physical oil, so it loses if the price falls; the short futures gain when the price falls.

check.q: The Q1 tenor falls to 34 EUR/MWh. What is the MtM of TTF-Q1?
check.a: (34 − 35) × 90,000 = −90,000 EUR (illustrative numbers): a loss, because Dana bought at 35.

check.q: Name five key fields of a trade.
check.a: Any five of: trade ID, direction (buy/sell), product, quantity and unit, price, delivery period and place, counterparty, book.

read_more: Dated Brent is the price assessment of physical North Sea cargoes published by Platts (→ L9); many North Sea and Atlantic Basin crudes are sold at Dated Brent plus or minus a differential. One ICE Brent futures contract is 1,000 barrels. TTF quarterly contracts (Q1 = January, February, March) are traded on ICE Endex and over the counter; in a non-leap year Q1 has 90 days. All prices, the differential and the delivery dates of Cargo NS-01 and TTF-Q1 are illustrative, and Northbridge is fictional. In the next modules you will see how these two trades are confirmed, priced over a pricing period, hedged with swaps, reported in the daily P&L and risk reports, and finally invoiced and settled.
